verdict.rationale: Restate's own durable execution journal stores completed steps and automatically resumes a failed invocation from where it left off. Operators can also inspect journals and manage invocations through the CLI. That covers the recover-from-recorded-history part of the story, but there is no evidence of an operator-initiated replay or rerun of a failed workflow, nor of restarting from a chosen step. missing for 10: documented manual rerun/replay command for failed invocations, restart-from-a-specific-step capability, debugging-oriented replay workflow, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I replay or rerun a failed workflow from its recorded history — optionally from a specific step — to debug and recover

citations.quote: Code automatically stores completed steps and resumes from where it left off when recovering from failures.
Full visibility into agent execution. Inspect journals, export traces, and cancel or kill stuck agents.
You can use the CLI to interact with Restate, and manage your services, deployments and invocations.
Each step is recorded for automatic recovery.
